signals.query: aws logs filter-log-events --region us-west-2 --log-group-name /aws/lambda/immix-autopatrol-schedule-cleanup --filter-pattern 'disabled admin schedule'
signals.description: Count of 'disabled admin schedule' log lines — actual PATCH fires against AutoPatrolSchedule.is_deleted=True. Post-flip (CLEANUP_ENABLED=true, 2026-04-23 17:59Z) this begins firing when a schedule is confirmed gone in Immix. Expected baseline: ~0 initially, small trickle as real stale schedules are caught. Spike >10/h = flap risk, stop and inspect. Manager-visible audit metric.

Schedules that REACHED THRESHOLD but were NOT disabled because Immix reports them as Active/Awaiting. Counted via 'anomaly: bucket=...' log lines. This is the safety-net firing: our connector says the schedule is gone, but Immix says it's live. Elevated rate indicates an ongoing mismatch — either our puller error classifier is wrong OR Immix is reporting stale status OR the schedule is genuinely flapping Active↔Paused. Pairs with actual_disable_rate: if disables=0 but anomaly is high, the safety net is absorbing everything (under-disabling the real stale set). Manager-visible: this quantifies 'Immix-side issues blocking cleanup'.

signals.query: aws logs filter-log-events --region us-west-2 --log-group-name /aws/lambda/immix-autopatrol-schedule-cleanup --start-time $(( $(date -u +%s) * 1000 - 7*86400*1000 )) --filter-pattern 'anomaly: bucket=' --query 'events[].message' --output text | grep -oE 'schedule [a-f0-9-]+' | sort | uniq -c | awk '$1 >= 2 {print}' | wc -l
signals.description: Count of DISTINCT schedule_ids that anomaly-reset 2+ times over 7 days. Non-zero means: the connector repeatedly believes a schedule is gone, but Immix repeatedly says active. Classic flappy-schedule / state-mismatch pattern — worth a targeted investigation into that specific schedule's Immix state vs our connector's state. Also surfaces Immix-side flake patterns (same schedule keeps reporting inconsistently). The single-count-unique signal (anomaly_reset_rate) tells you IF there's a problem; this one tells you WHERE to look.

signals.nrql: SELECT uniqueCount(container_name) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND message='WARNING:(MainThread):No models configured for site, appending dummy model.' AND container_name LIKE '%-autopatrol-%' SINCE 24 hours ago
signals.description: Distinct AUTOPATROL connector containers logging the dummy-model fallback warning. >0 means an AutoPatrol site has empty `models` in settings.json and is silently running a no-op model. AUTO-566 (config-sync gap) is the underlying fix; this signal makes the misconfiguration discoverable proactively. **Filter `container_name LIKE '%-autopatrol-%'` is critical** — VCH and CHM integration types are not meant to run models, so the warning firing on them is expected/benign noise. Use exact-equality match on the message — fleet-wide `LIKE %...%` queries on message time out at NRDB scope.

signals.nrql: SELECT uniqueCount(podName) FROM K8sPodSample WHERE clusterName='Connector-EKS' AND status='Pending' SINCE 5 minutes ago
signals.description: Pods stuck in Pending. Non-zero = scheduler can't place / no capacity / image pull stuck / unsatisfiable affinity. Brief blips during deploy churn are normal; sustained >0 is a problem. Initial threshold 2026-04-27: observed 39 baseline, set conservative thresholds to avoid daily-yellow noise; tighten after 14d of sink data.
signals.would_have_caught: Capacity-pressure incidents where deploys can't start

signals.nrql: SELECT uniqueCount(nodeName) FROM K8sNodeSample WHERE clusterName='Connector-EKS' SINCE 5 minutes ago
signals.description: Total node count in the cluster. Drift outside expected range = autoscaler runaway, ghost nodes, capacity drop. Initial calibration 2026-04-27: 110 nodes baseline. Thresholds: yellow if drops below 80 (~25%), red below 50 (~50%); also yellow if exceeds 200 (autoscaler runaway).
signals.would_have_caught: Autoscaler / capacity drift detection

signals.nrql: SELECT uniqueCount(nodeName) FROM K8sNodeSample WHERE clusterName='Connector-EKS' AND condition='Ready' AND status!='True' SINCE 5 minutes ago
signals.description: Nodes reporting Ready != True. Single NotReady can be drain prep; sustained or multiple = real capacity problem (workloads will start evicting).
signals.would_have_caught: Node-failure cascades before workloads notice

signals.nrql: SELECT sum(deploymentDesiredReplicas - deploymentAvailableReplicas) FROM K8sDeploymentSample WHERE clusterName='Connector-EKS' SINCE 5 minutes ago
signals.description: Sum of (desired - available) replicas across all deployments. >0 means some deployment can't reach its target replica count — image pull failure, crashloop, anti-affinity stuck, capacity. Brief positive during rolling deploys is normal.
signals.would_have_caught: Deployment stuck-at-replica-N regressions

signals.nrql: SELECT max(restartCount) - min(restartCount) FROM K8sContainerSample WHERE clusterName='Connector-EKS' SINCE 5 minutes ago
signals.description: Restart-count delta over a 5-min window. Fan-out cousin of fleet_oomkills_24h — catches crashloop bursts in real time vs. the 24h aggregate. NB: this is a single max-min across the fleet, not a sum; calibrate after observing real distribution. NRDB has no now() function so the original 'count restarts since now()-5m' formulation didn't work.
signals.would_have_caught: Real-time crashloop detection (5m granularity vs. fleet_oomkills_24h). DISABLED 2026-04-27 pending NRQL design + threshold calibration; see cookbook §Per-source recipes for derivative-based alternatives.

signals.command: python ssl.create_default_context() + getpeercert() per host; days until cert.notAfter
signals.description: Days until each customer-facing HTTPS endpoint's TLS cert expires. FACET dict {host: days_remaining}. Add a host by appending its FQDN to the `hosts` list — the collector iterates and emits one entry per host. Threshold yellow_below=21 (3-week warning), red_below=7 (week-out scramble). Day-1 (2026-04-29): all 4 monitored hosts >100 days. Add more hosts as new endpoints come online (e.g. signal.actuate.ai, customer-specific subdomains). Hosts that fail to connect (DNS / firewall / wrong port) emit null and surface as classification 'error' so you notice the misconfig.
signals.would_have_caught: Customer-facing endpoint cert expiry — first time we get to find out before the customer does.

signals.description: Failed user-systemd units on the minipc. Returns FACET dict {unit_name: 1} so detail page lists exactly WHICH units are failing. Standing alarm — any non-empty result is yellow, multiple is red.
signals.would_have_caught: Silent failure of any timer-driven unit (rebuild-blog, run-dashboard-check, etc.)

signals.description: Failed system-wide units on the minipc (caddy, docker, tailscaled, etc.). Same shape as the user variant. systemd-networkd-wait-online tends to flap on boot — mask it via phase script if it's the only chronic offender.
signals.would_have_caught: Caddy / Docker / Tailscaled drops

signals.command: journalctl --user -u <units> --since 24 hours ago | count Started lines
signals.description: How many times the minipc's tracked timers fired in the last 24h. Sum across minipc-app, rebuild-blog, rebuild-quartz, run-dashboard-check, collect-repos. Normal: ~336 (every 5 min × 5 timers ÷ 30s grace). Drops indicate timer wedge or daemon-reload not picking up. Initial threshold conservative; recalibrate after 7d.
signals.would_have_caught: Timer wedge / linger lost / user session not active

signals.command: parse pyproject.toml + requirements.txt for actuate-frames pin spec
signals.description: Per-repo pin spec for `actuate-frames`. FACET dict {repo_name: pin_spec} — only repos that actually pin the package show up. Drift detector: when this dict has more than one distinct value, repos are pinning different versions. Workspace declarations skipped. Informational by design — version strings can't classify; the `new_pattern` regression rule will flag when a new repo starts pinning or a version moves.
signals.would_have_caught: Library-pin drift: e.g. one repo on 1.x while sibling repo bumps to 2.x without the consumer updating.

signals.command: parse pyproject.toml + requirements.txt for actuate-filters pin spec
signals.description: Per-repo pin spec for `actuate-filters`. Same shape as repo_actuate_frames_pin. As of seed-day 2026-04-28 there's already drift: vms-connector pins `==2.0.4` while actuate_admin pins `~=2.0.0` — useful first datapoint for the signal's value.
signals.would_have_caught: vms-connector / actuate_admin diverging on actuate-filters — caught at the moment a downstream consumer bumps without coordinating.

signals.command: parse pyproject.toml + requirements.txt for actuate-pullers pin spec
signals.description: Per-repo pin spec for `actuate-pullers`. Same shape as repo_actuate_frames_pin. As of seed-day 2026-04-28 only vms-connector pins it — kept enabled so future consumers (e.g. autopatrol-server, actuate-inference-api) appear automatically when they adopt.
signals.would_have_caught: Adoption-tracking — a new repo pinning actuate-pullers shows up via the `new_pattern` rule.

signals.description: Cyclomatic-complexity hotspots (grade C and worse, CCN >= 11) per repo. Tracks the count of functions/methods that need refactoring attention. FACET dict {repo_name: count}. Initial baseline 2026-04-29: actuate-libraries=165, actuate_admin=119, vms-connector=92, autopatrol-server=37; smaller repos in single digits. Thresholds anchored to those baselines — recalibrate after 7d.
signals.would_have_caught: Sustained complexity-debt accrual: a refactor PR that nets +20 hotspots without intent.

signals.description: Count of F401 (unused import) violations per repo. Captures dead imports left behind after refactors — usually a 1-line fix per finding. FACET dict {repo_name: count}. Day-1 baselines (2026-04-29): actuate_admin=265, actuate-libraries=172, vms-connector=110, autopatrol-server=33, connector_deployer=5, autopatrol_onboarder=5, actuate-inference-api=0. Thresholds set so admin's existing debt is yellow (visible) without going straight to red.
signals.would_have_caught: Lint-debt drift; an import that survived a refactor will show up the next collect.

signals.command: git for-each-ref refs/remotes/origin/ --format='... %(committerdate:unix)' | count refs older than 60d
signals.description: Per-repo count of remote branches whose last commit is older than 60 days. Pure local git, no API call. Captures branch-debt — abandoned features, codex/cursor automation rot, etc. Day-1 example: queue_consumer has 68 stale branches against 77 total (codex/cursor automation residue). FACET dict {repo_name: count}.
signals.would_have_caught: Branch-bloat that would otherwise stay invisible — only the active branches show on /app/repos/.

signals.command: gh run list --limit 50 --json conclusion -R <slug>; pct fail/(fail+ok)
signals.description: Percentage of recent CI workflow runs that ended in failure (last 50 runs). Counts conclusion in {failure, timed_out, startup_failure} as fail; counts {success} as ok. Skipped/cancelled/in-progress are excluded from the denominator. Day-1 distribution (2026-04-29): most repos 0-15%, actuate_ailink the obvious outlier at 38% — broken pipeline. Threshold yellow=10 catches chronic mid-tier debt; red=25 flags actively broken CI. Returns None for repos with no CI runs (drops from FACET).
signals.would_have_caught: Sustained CI flake or broken pipeline — would have caught actuate_ailink's 38% rate immediately.

signals.command: gh pr list --state open --limit 50 --json createdAt -R <slug>; median age in days
signals.description: Median age across each repo's currently-open PRs. Pairs with `repo_mtm_days_p50` (merged latency) for a flow picture: high MTM + high open-PR-age = review bottleneck; high MTM + low open-PR-age = recent spike. Repos with zero open PRs drop from the FACET dict (uninteresting / clean). 1 gh API call per repo per collect (16/h, well under rate limit).
signals.would_have_caught: Sustained review-bottleneck where PRs queue up days before being looked at.

signals.command: gh pr list --state merged --limit 50 --json mergedAt,createdAt -R <slug>; median delta in days
signals.description: Median time-to-merge across the last 50 merged PRs per repo, in days. Resolves the GitHub slug from each repo's `git config remote.origin.url`. FACET dict {repo_name: float days}. Day-1 baseline (2026-04-29): vms-connector p50 = 0.41 days (~10h). Slow-down indicator: if a team is hitting review or CI-flake bottlenecks, the median creeps up. Fast-down indicator: a flurry of stage-bot autobumps drops the median; that's healthy noise. 1 gh API call per repo per collect (7/h, well under 5000/h limit).
signals.would_have_caught: Sustained CI flake or review-bottleneck regression — visible as p50 climbing over 7d.

signals.description: Likely-unused functions, classes, vars per repo at >=80% vulture confidence. The default 60% bucket is dominated by Django framework FPs (Meta classes, migrations, apps.py, model field declarations, enum members) — see [[2026-04-29_minipc-api-surface]] / collect.py for the FP-cut analysis. Bumping to 80% drops actuate_admin from 3308 to 41 (98% noise reduction) while preserving rank order across all 16 repos. Day-1 baselines (2026-04-29 conf80): connector_deployer=45, actuate-libraries=45, actuate_admin=41, vms-connector=34, actuate-watchman=22, queue_consumer=11, actuate_ailink=8, autopatrol-server=8, autopatrol_onboarder=6, actuate_monitoring_api=6, ds-terraform-eks-v2=3, others=0-2. Thresholds set at ~2x current top-of-set so a real refactor regression flags but normal scale doesn't.
signals.would_have_caught: Dead-code accrual after a refactor — flagged via baseline_drift on next collect.

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name='clips-prod' SINCE 12 hours ago
signals.description: Total log volume for clips-prod. High-throughput service with clear day/night bimodal pattern (7d range 8.5M-24.6M). Silent-drop rule catches stopping entirely; baseline_drift will catch pattern shift.

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND (message LIKE '%AccessDeniedException%' OR message LIKE '%is not authorized to perform%' OR message LIKE '%not authorized to perform%') FACET container_name SINCE 12 hours ago LIMIT 10
signals.description: Cluster-wide IAM AccessDenied detector. Counts AccessDeniedException + 'not authorized to perform' message patterns across all Connector-EKS containers, faceted by container. IAM denials are NEVER a normal steady state — any non-zero count means a service is missing a permission grant (new GSI, new resource, role drift). Caught the 2026-04-29 autopatrol-microservice-role MotionFrame/index/run_timestamp gap retroactively; a yellow_above=1 threshold means the next instance flags within 12h instead of waiting for a manual overnight check.
signals.would_have_caught: 2026-04-29 autopatrol-microservice-role MotionFrame GSI denial (~27 hits in 12h before fix; would have flagged on first hit)
